$comment: Template for the local benchmark corpus manifest. Copy it to <app_data>/bench/corpus/corpus.json (Windows: %APPDATA%\com.sigil.app\bench\corpus\corpus.json) and list the clips stored next to it. The corpus holds consented recordings of real people: it lives only on your PC and is never committed or uploaded. Specs reference a clip with an input such as {"kind": "wav", "path": "corpus/clips/speech-01.wav"} (IPC specs resolve paths against <app_data>/bench/; CLI specs against the spec file's folder, so use an absolute path there). Synthetic stand-ins for every kind can be written with scripts/bench/make-test-clips.py.
name: local
description: 20 consented speech clips (VRChat-style mic, several speakers and languages), the same clips with world-music bleed at -20 dB, and a singing set.

defaults.level: as recorded (do not normalize; the harness measures real mic levels)

clips.speaker: S1
clips.notes: speech-01 mixed with VRChat world music at -20 dB (make-test-clips.py --mix can make a synthetic stand-in).

clips.speaker: S3
clips.notes: Sustained notes and a scale (F0 range and pitch-error checks).
